title: PCB bioleaching: feedstocks and a strain-binding error

steps.title: Separate feed composition from recovery
steps.question: What does Table 1 measure?
steps.look: Gate accepts Au, Cu and Ni content in the two feedstocks: three metal rows and two sample columns.
steps.boundary: These six composition cells describe the feed, not six bioleaching recovery results.

steps.title: Inspect the PCB gold-content cell
steps.question: Which feedstock owns 0.0038 ± 0.0002?
steps.look: The phone-PCB column supplies 0.0038 ± 0.0002% Au by mass. The extracted CONTAINS record keeps the cell and uncertainty.
steps.boundary: This is initial content, not gold recovery. Matching metal names alone cannot combine different feedstocks.

steps.title: Expose the single-strain binding error
steps.question: Does the Relation candidate preserve the right subject?
steps.look: The 42% candidate labels its experiment group as MXPE6 alone, but its Process subject and Setting refer to the combined-strain route.
steps.boundary: The highlighted sentence contradicts that subject. An archived single_shot_verified label is not proof of semantic correctness.

steps.title: Do not claim an unperformed revision
steps.question: Did Process Revision fix the strain assignment?
steps.look: The reconciliation log reports a skipped, uncommitted revision with zero LLM calls and zero applied operations.
steps.boundary: A populated Setting is not necessarily the correct Setting. This archive records no committed repair of the 42% binding.

steps.title: Attach scope: identify the phone-derived feedstock
steps.question: What material was actually sampled?
steps.look: After document merge and revision, Scope adds source context. Scope identifies a batch of cellular-phone PCBs, hand-cut to approximately 1 × 1 cm pieces. Inspect its archived preparation evidence.
steps.boundary: The PCB is the feedstock, not the whole phone. Markdown escape differences can be normalized for navigation; no archived quotation is rewritten. Scope is post-merge provenance, not an upstream extraction input.

steps.title: Attach scope: keep the second feedstock distinct
steps.question: Are computer goldfingers the same sample?
steps.look: After document merge and revision, Scope adds source context. A separate Scope describes gold-plated finger integrated circuits, cut to 0.850 mm. They remain a different Component from phone PCBs.
steps.boundary: The source uses GFICMs; the table's second header is transcribed GFMBCs. Original text and archived labels remain inspectable. Scope is post-merge provenance, not an upstream extraction input.

steps.title: Compare the goldfinger composition
steps.question: Does the second feedstock retain its own measurement?
steps.look: The final goldfinger → Au relation retains 0.0607 ± 0.0001%, linked to the other column in Table 1.
steps.boundary: Different feedstock composition is not evidence of different process recovery. No values are pooled here.

steps.title: Read the combined-strain result
steps.question: Who achieved 87% gold recovery?
steps.look: The source attributes 87% Au recovery from PCBs to the combination of both Aspergillus strains. The final combined-strain Process agrees on this result.
steps.boundary: The same sentence also reports 42% for MXPE6 alone. The earlier Relation inspection showed the single-strain binding error; correct extraction of 87% does not validate 42%.

steps.title: Check whether the error survived merge
steps.question: Was 42% corrected in the final output?
steps.look: No: 42% still has the same combined-strain Process and Setting as 87%, despite its single-strain experiment group.
steps.boundary: Both numbers are reported correctly, but one treatment assignment is wrong. The replay exposes the error without editing frozen predictions.

steps.title: Trace the questionable graph observation
steps.question: Does fusion remove the binding error?
steps.look: Open the combined-strain Process's Au observations, choose 42%, then View evidence in replay. Compare the source's MXPE6-only wording.
steps.boundary: Fusion retains this archived assignment; it does not validate or correct it. Provenance lets the viewer inspect the disagreement.
